question: After you cut a clip, or lift a stretch out of it, what does the part after the cut say on the timeline?
context: The cut walkthrough mock labels the second half of a blade cut screen-recording · 2. The app labels every part with the plain clip name, for Command K and, since today, for Lift too (it used to say Sample Talk copy).

options.label: Both parts show the clip name
options.summary: Both parts read Sample Talk, the way the app shows it today. Premiere and Final Cut do the same.
pros: What a Premiere or Final Cut editor already sees
Nothing changes when you cut, so the timeline stays calm
cons: Not what the cut mock draws
Two parts with the same name cannot be told apart by their label
options.mitigation: Picking a part still shows its own in and out in the panel.

options.label: The part after the cut adds a number
options.summary: The first part reads Sample Talk and the part after the cut reads Sample Talk · 2, then · 3, as the cut mock draws it, for Command K, Lift and Extract alike.
pros: Each part can be told apart and talked about
cons: The numbers can look like separate copies, which is the confusion this task fixed
Numbers shift when parts are reordered or deleted
options.mitigation: The number is only a label on the bar; the clip keeps one name everywhere else.
